facts.text: Allerton began as a 3,800‑acre tract purchased by Samuel Allerton in 1880, laying the groundwork for the village that would follow.
When the Chicago & Eastern Illinois railroad arrived, Allerton granted a right‑of‑way, built a grain elevator, bank, school, and installed a water system.
The village sits in Sidell Township of Vermilion County, with a small slice spilling into neighboring Champaign County.
Samuel Allerton, a prominent Vermilion County landowner, made his fortune trading agricultural products and livestock across the Midwest.
His 12,000‑acre Piatt County holdings later became Robert Allerton Park, a notable green space west of Monticello.
Across four Midwest states, Samuel Allerton controlled roughly 78,000 acres, making him one of the era’s largest landholders.
